newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ING BARINGS UPGRADES IAS FORECAST FOR BORSODCHEM.
newsitem.headline: ING BARINGS UPGRADES IAS FORECAST FOR BORSODCHEM.

text.p: ING Barings has revised its IAS forecast for Borsodchem upwards following the recent release of the Hungarian chemical firm's 1H consolidated IAS results, the securities house said in a valuation update.
In the update ING Barings rated the shares as "long-term buy".

"Based on the new figures Borsodchem reported net profit of 3,596 million forints in 1H 1996, 6.9 percent higher than the HAS figures of 3,362 million forints," ING Barings' analysts Gabor Sitanyi and Barna Papay said.
HAS stands for Hungarian Accounting Standards.

"Our recent meeting with the management confirmed some major long-term accounting differences between HAS and IAS and consequently we are upgrading our IAS forecast of 6,351 million forints to 6,930 million forints," they said.
Borsodchem is expected to take advantage from opportunities in the construction sector and in infrastructure in Eastern Europe, too, they said.

"As a result of the more buoyant outlook for the construction industry in Eastern Europe and also given the transportation limit of 500 km Borsodchem is well-positioned to benefit from demand related to infrastructure projects in the region," the analysts said.
The new forecast is backed not only by Borsodchem's recently signed PVC contracts, but also by the company's previously conservative provisioning.
"According to the management the company is likely to write back some major provisions to its 1996 IAS profits totalling 600 to 650 million forints this year," they said.
In addition, the company is still the only licencee of methylene dyphenil diisocyanate (MDI) in Eastern Europe which provides a good hedge against the PVC cycle, they said.
